title: EEG-based detection of early functional brain changes in subjective cognitive decline: a prospective cohort study
summary: In a prospective multicenter cohort of 120 people with subjective cognitive decline followed for two years, longitudinal EEG measures were associated with amyloid status and cognitive change; machine-learning analysis found predictive information beyond standard clinical variables. The cohort included only 24 amyloid-positive participants, and the authors note possible optimism because nested cross-validation was not used.
ai_technology: Interpretable machine learning analyzes longitudinal EEG features to identify amyloid burden and cognitive change in subjective cognitive decline.
organization: Department of Neurology, Eunpyeong St. Mary's Hospital, The Catholic University of Korea, Seoul, South Korea; Department of Applied Artificial Intelligence, Hanyang University, Ansan, South Korea; Department of Neurology, Seoul St. Mary's Hospital, The Catholic University of Korea, Seoul, South Korea; Department of Neurology, Uijeongbu St. Mary's Hospital, The Catholic University of Korea, Uijeongbu City, South Korea

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; publication date and first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: Longitudinal EEG features were analyzed against amyloid and cognitive outcomes over two years; model performance was internally estimated.
evidence.unknown: Only 24 amyloid-positive participants; nested cross-validation was not used and independent external validation was not reported.
evidence.ai_role: Interpretable machine learning analyzes longitudinal EEG features to identify amyloid burden and cognitive change in subjective cognitive decline.
